findings.rule: REVIEW.md framework rule: 'plan.md must reflect the diff ... a diff that departs from the plan without a plan.md update in the same commit is non-compliant'; coding-standards rule 3 ('the diff stays inside plan.md's Files that change; a departure updates plan.md in the same commit')
findings.summary: The diff imports `shell_guard` at module scope in tests/test_hooks.py, but plan.md's Order of work step 1 and Files-that-change section require it 'imported inside the test functions, never at module top-level, so a failure in the new tests cannot abort collection of the rest of the file', and plan.md was never updated in any commit on this branch to reflect the departure.

`_absolute_rule_root` is left in production code but, after `ci_settings_file` was rewritten to call `_posix_root(root_resolved.as_posix())` directly, it has no remaining production caller (only tests/test_ci.py:189,596 still call it).
The new hook script is 985 lines, nearly double the coding-standards check's 500-line advisory threshold for a single source file.

Since `FRAMEWORK_SUITE` (line 32) is now itself `tuple(p.name for p in run.discover(FRAMEWORK_CASES))`, the pre-existing assertion `names == list(FRAMEWORK_SUITE)` compares `run.discover`'s output against itself and is tautological — a bug in `run.discover` (e.g. a skipped or duplicated case folder) would no longer be caught by this line, though each case is still individually validated below it.
